source_observations.observation: Yad, tad and etad give relative and deictic quantities. Pramāṇa differs from parimāṇa. Separate senses preserve the measure suffixes and their possible nesting. A Vedic supplement admits personal-pronoun similarity.
The substitution for v after kim and idam signals the affix’s availability. Alternatively split the rule into affix licensing followed by substitution.
Inquiry about a determining number permits ḍati or vatup. A dismissive question about an already supplied ten fails the numerical-inquiry condition.

source_observations.observation: Idam and kim take their own īś/kī replacements under the stated suffix conditions.
Masculine singular markers of relative and corresponding quantity qualify artha. The second clause supplies its sense by correlation.
Etāvān is masculine singular with mahimā. Asya supplies a genitive. The following comparative refers separately to puruṣa.
The nasalized contextual spelling before anyaḥ has nominative tvāvān in the Pada. The addressee is Indra.
The qualified genitive tvāvataḥ is explained as of one like you, hence of you here. Vayam controls the first-person plural smasi.
Māvataḥ describes the sacrificing speaker in the genitive. The commentator explicitly invokes the two-pronoun Vedic resemblance supplement.
Kiyān qualifies the value of a harmful religious practice. It does not request a count of discrete items.
Iyān refers to the extent of the artha of embodied beings. It has the same masculine head noun as the question in the other chapter.
Kati asks the count. Yāvantaḥ agrees with the gods named in the litany. A later katame asks which ones. Repeated katy eva represents one case.
In the Vedic environment an i is added at the end of mas. The RV and Sāyaṇa establish the actual token and its first-plural interpretation.
The Pada separates upa and iyāt in the alternative ritual instruction. The second word is verbal and does not belong to the idam quantity relation.
